title: L1: surface behavioral coupling in review output
description: Add behavioral coupling warnings to review output. When a changed file has co-change partners above the Jaccard threshold with no static import edge, surface them: "your change touched A; B is behaviorally coupled and may need changes too." Depends on the commit_files table and co-change infrastructure from sutra/67.

acceptance_criteria.text: Review output includes a behavioral_coupling key (or similar) listing co-change partners of changed files that lack static edges
Each entry shows the partner file, Jaccard coefficient, and shared commit count
Only pairs above the configured cochange_threshold are included
Behavioral coupling partners appear in recommended_reads if not already present

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review — verdict: needs-attention

[medium] Behavioral coupling filter does not exclude all static reference edges (src/tools/review.rs:807-825)
The review output filters "hidden" partners using only import_edges. Clustering defines static edges from resolved symbol refs, so call/use refs without an import row still count as static edges for clustering but are reported here as behavioral coupling. This can send reviewers to already-statically-linked files as if they were hidden coupling. Same pattern appears in orient (sutra/81). Recommend building the exclusion set from the same resolved-reference graph used by clustering: map all_resolved_refs() through all_symbol_file_map() into canonical file pairs.
